findings.evidence:
`pkg/store/helper/helper.go:912` `SyncTableSchemaToTiFlash` calls `util.InternalHTTPClient().Get(...)` then immediately `resp.Body.Close()` and returns `nil` without checking `resp.StatusCode` or response body.
`http.Client.Get` only errors on transport; non-2xx (e.g. 404/500) will still return `resp, nil`.
Second confirmation: mock TiFlash status server in `pkg/domain/infosync/tiflash_manager.go:407` only registers `/tiflash/sync-status/...` and `/config` (no `/tiflash/sync-schema/...`), implying a 404 is plausible and would be silently treated as success.
Caller treats schema-sync failure as fatal in the vector index DDL flow (`pkg/ddl/index.go:819` calls `infosync.SyncTiFlashTableSchema(...)` and returns error on failure), so false-success can advance the job into progress polling even if schema sync didn’t happen.
findings.fix: Check `resp.StatusCode` and return an error on non-2xx (optionally include a small response-body prefix for diagnostics). If forward-compat needs to tolerate missing endpoints, explicitly special-case expected codes (e.g. 404) with a warning log and/or fallback to the legacy URL, rather than treating all non-2xx as success.
findings.impact: If TiFlash returns non-2xx (endpoint missing/version mismatch, internal error, auth/rate-limit), TiDB will incorrectly assume schema sync succeeded. For vector index DDL, this can lead to stuck/slow DDL reorg (polling progress that never starts) and harder-to-diagnose failures; in worst cases it can block the DDL job queue behind a non-progressing job.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master:pkg/store/helper/helper.go` (fetched from `upstream`): `SyncTableSchemaToTiFlash` still closes the body and returns `nil` without status/body validation.
findings.verify: Add a targeted unit/integration test where the TiFlash status endpoint returns a non-2xx for `/tiflash/sync-schema/...` and assert `infosync.SyncTiFlashTableSchema` surfaces an error (or, if you intentionally tolerate specific codes, assert it logs and takes the intended fallback path). Also validate vector-index DDL doesn’t advance `SnapshotVer`/progress polling on a sync failure.
findings.what: `SyncTableSchemaToTiFlash` treats any HTTP response as success (no `StatusCode`/body check), so schema-sync failures can be silently ignored and the vector-index DDL flow can proceed into an invalid state.
